review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

11:1.sourceText: Ἦν δέ τις ἀσθενῶν, Λάζαρος ἀπὸ Βηθανίας, ἐκ τῆς κώμης Μαρίας καὶ Μάρθας τῆς ἀδελφῆς αὐτῆς.
11:1.targetText: At this time a man named Lazarus was sick. He lived in Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.

groups.note: The connective δέ opening the new episode is rendered At this time.
ἀπό ("from") is rendered lived in.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB's apposition (Bethany, the village of …) leaves ἐκ ("from") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the name; the Greek sets Λάζαρος beside "a certain sick man".
English starts a new sentence with a supplied subject.

11:2.sourceText: ἦν δὲ Μαριὰμ ἡ ἀλείψασα τὸν Κύριον μύρῳ καὶ ἐκμάξασα τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς, ἧς ὁ ἀδελφὸς Λάζαρος ἠσθένει.
11:2.targetText: (Mary, whose brother Lazarus was sick, was to anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair.)

groups.note: ἡ ἀλείψασα ("the one who anointed") is rendered was to anoint, since the anointing is told in 12:3.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated and sets the verse in parentheses.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:3.sourceText: ἀπέστειλαν οὖν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσαι Κύριε, ἴδε ὃν φιλεῖς ἀσθενεῖ.
11:3.targetText: So the sisters sent word to Jesus, “Lord, the one You love is sick.”

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name Jesus.
The participle λέγουσαι ("saying") is folded into sent word.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἴδε ("look") untranslated.

11:4.sourceText: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Αὕτη ἡ ἀσθένεια οὐκ ἔστιν πρὸς θάνατον ἀλλ’ ὑπὲρ τῆς δόξης τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ δι’ αὐτῆς.
11:4.targetText: When Jesus heard this, He said, “This sickness will not end in death. No, it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσας ("having heard") is rendered as a When-clause.
οὐκ ἔστιν πρὸς θάνατον ("is not toward death") is rendered will not end in death.
ἀλλά ("but") is rendered No, stressing the contrast.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of hearing.
English supplies a subject and verb for the elliptical phrase.

11:5.sourceText: ἠγάπα δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον.
11:5.targetText: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:6.sourceText: ὡς οὖν ἤκουσεν ὅτι ἀσθενεῖ, τότε μὲν ἔμεινεν ἐν ᾧ ἦν τόπῳ δύο ἡμέρας·
11:6.targetText: So on hearing that Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was for two days,

groups.note: ἐν ᾧ … τόπῳ ("in the place in which") is rendered where.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τότε μέν ("then") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject of ἀσθενεῖ ("he is sick").

11:7.sourceText: ἔπειτα μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς Ἄγωμεν εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν πάλιν.
11:7.targetText: and then He said to the disciples, “Let us go back to Judea.”

groups.note: ἔπειτα μετὰ τοῦτο ("then after this") is rendered and then.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:8.sourceText: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί Ῥαββεί, νῦν ἐζήτουν σε λιθάσαι οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ πάλιν ὑπάγεις ἐκεῖ;
11:8.targetText: “Rabbi,” they replied, “the Jews just tried to stone You, and You are going back there?”

groups.note: οἱ μαθηταί ("the disciples") is rendered they.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.

11:9.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Οὐχὶ δώδεκα ὧραί εἰσιν τῆς ἡμέρας; ἐάν τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, οὐ προσκόπτει, ὅτι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου τούτου βλέπει·
11:9.targetText: Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours of daylight? If anyone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.

groups.note: βλέπει τὸ φῶς ("sees the light") is rendered sees by the light.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:10.sourceText: ἐὰν δέ τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ νυκτί, προσκόπτει, ὅτι τὸ φῶς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐτῷ.
11:10.targetText: But if anyone walks at night, he will stumble, because he has no light.”

groups.note: τὸ φῶς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐτῷ ("the light is not in him") is recast as he has no light.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:11.sourceText: ταῦτα εἶπεν, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει αὐτοῖς Λάζαρος ὁ φίλος ἡμῶν κεκοίμηται· ἀλλὰ πορεύομαι ἵνα ἐξυπνίσω αὐτόν.
11:11.targetText: After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”

groups.note: μετὰ τοῦτο ("after this") is rendered After, joining the two clauses.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes the first clause a time clause, so καί is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the destination.

11:12.sourceText: εἶπαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτῷ Κύριε, εἰ κεκοίμηται, σωθήσεται.
11:12.targetText: His disciples replied, “Lord, if he is sleeping, he will get better.”

groups.note: The article οἱ with μαθηταί is rendered His.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.
The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.

11:13.sourceText: εἰρήκει δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς περὶ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ· ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἔδοξαν ὅτι περὶ τῆς κοιμήσεως τοῦ ὕπνου λέγει.
11:13.targetText: They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep, but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus in the first English clause and renders ὁ Ἰησοῦς here as He.
The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered of Lazarus.
τῆς κοιμήσεως τοῦ ὕπνου ("the rest of sleep") is rendered actual sleep.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB reverses the two clauses and renders the contrast once, with but.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject of λέγει; the Greek gives it only in the verb.

11:14.sourceText: τότε οὖν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς παρρησίᾳ Λάζαρος ἀπέθανεν,
11:14.targetText: So Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τότε ("then") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:15.sourceText: καὶ χαίρω δι’ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα πιστεύσητε, ὅτι οὐκ ἤμην ἐκεῖ· ἀλλὰ ἄγωμεν πρὸς αὐτόν.
11:15.targetText: and for your sake I am glad I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ὅτι ("that") unexpressed: I am glad I was not there.

11:16.sourceText: εἶπεν οὖν Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος τοῖς συνμαθηταῖς Ἄγωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἵνα ἀποθάνωμεν μετ’ αὐτοῦ.
11:16.targetText: Then Thomas called Didymus said to his fellow disciples, “Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.”

groups.note: The article τοῖς is rendered his.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The explicit ἡμεῖς ("we") is rendered us in Let us also go.

11:17.sourceText: Ἐλθὼν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εὗρεν αὐτὸν τέσσαρας ἤδη ἡμέρας ἔχοντα ἐν τῷ μνημείῳ.
11:17.targetText: When Jesus arrived, He found that Lazarus had already spent four days in the tomb.

groups.note: The participle ἐλθών ("having come") is rendered as a When-clause.
The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name Lazarus.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the clause that follows found.

11:18.sourceText: ἦν δὲ Βηθανία ἐγγὺς τῶν Ἱεροσολύμων ὡς ἀπὸ σταδίων δεκαπέντε.
11:18.targetText: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, a little less than two miles away,

targetPhrases.text: a little less than two miles

groups.note: ὡς … σταδίων δεκαπέντε ("about fifteen stadia") is converted to English measure.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:19.sourceText: πολλοὶ δὲ ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐληλύθεισαν πρὸς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ Μαριὰμ, ἵνα παραμυθήσωνται αὐτὰς περὶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ.
11:19.targetText: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them in the loss of their brother.

groups.note: περί ("concerning") is rendered in the loss of.
The article τοῦ is rendered their.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:20.sourceText: ἡ οὖν Μάρθα ὡς ἤκουσεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἔρχεται, ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ· Μαριὰμ δὲ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ ἐκαθέζετο.
11:20.targetText: So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet Him; but Mary stayed at home.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:21.sourceText: εἶπεν οὖν ἡ Μάρθα πρὸς Ἰησοῦν Κύριε, εἰ ἦς ὧδε, οὐκ ἂν ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός μου.
11:21.targetText: Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:22.sourceText: καὶ νῦν οἶδα ὅτι ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσῃ τὸν Θεὸν δώσει σοι ὁ Θεός.
11:22.targetText: But even now I know that God will give You whatever You ask of Him.”

groups.note: BSB renders τὸν Θεόν ("God") as Him, since God is named earlier in the sentence.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here, rendered But.

11:23.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀναστήσεται ὁ ἀδελφός σου.
11:23.targetText: “Your brother will rise again,” Jesus told her.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:24.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα Οἶδα ὅτι ἀναστήσεται ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
11:24.targetText: Martha replied, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:25.sourceText: εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή· ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ κἂν ἀποθάνῃ ζήσεται,
11:25.targetText: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:26.sourceText: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ζῶν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· πιστεύεις τοῦτο;
11:26.targetText: And everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die. Do you believe this?”

groups.note: οὐ μή … εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ("not … forever") is rendered never.

11:27.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ Ναί, Κύριε· ἐγὼ πεπίστευκα ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐρχόμενος.
11:27.targetText: “Yes, Lord,” she answered, “I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world.”

groups.note: ὁ … ἐρχόμενος ("the one coming") is rendered who was to come.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:28.sourceText: καὶ τοῦτο εἰποῦσα ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἐφώνησεν Μαριὰμ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς λάθρᾳ εἰποῦσα Ὁ Διδάσκαλος πάρεστιν καὶ φωνεῖ σε.
11:28.targetText: After Martha had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside to tell her, “The Teacher is here and is asking for you.”

groups.note: The participle εἰποῦσα ("having said") is rendered as an After-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject of the participle.
English supplies the object of tell.

11:29.sourceText: ἐκείνη δὲ ὡς ἤκουσεν, ἐγείρεται ταχὺ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν·
11:29.targetText: And when Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to Him.

groups.note: BSB's Greek has a different form of the same verb here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject of ἤκουσεν; the Greek gives it as ἐκείνη ("she") with the main verb.
English supplies the object of hearing.

11:30.sourceText: οὔπω δὲ ἐληλύθει ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν κώμην, ἀλλ’ ἦν ἔτι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα.
11:30.targetText: Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met Him.

groups.note: ἐληλύθει εἰς ("had come into") is rendered had entered.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:31.sourceText: οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι οἱ ὄντες μετ’ αὐτῆς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ παραμυθούμενοι αὐτήν, ἰδόντες τὴν Μαριὰμ ὅτι ταχέως ἀνέστη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν, ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῇ, δόξαντες ὅτι ὑπάγει εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον ἵνα κλαύσῃ ἐκεῖ.
11:31.targetText: When the Jews who were in the house consoling Mary saw how quickly she got up and went out, they followed her, supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn there.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτήν ("her") is rendered by the name Mary.
The participle ἰδόντες ("having seen") is rendered as a When-clause.
Μαριάμ, the object of saw, is rendered as the subject she of the clause that follows.
ὅτι ("that") is rendered how.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.
BSB leaves μετ’ αὐτῆς ("with her") unexpressed.
BSB joins the two descriptions without and.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ὅτι ("that") unexpressed after supposing.

11:32.sourceText: ἡ οὖν Μαριὰμ ὡς ἦλθεν ὅπου ἦν Ἰησοῦς, ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἔπεσεν αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς πόδας, λέγουσα αὐτῷ Κύριε, εἰ ἦς ὧδε, οὐκ ἄν μου ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός.
11:32.targetText: When Mary came to Jesus and saw Him, she fell at His feet and said, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”

groups.note: ὅπου ἦν ("where … was") is rendered to: came to Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἰδοῦσα ("seeing") to the When-clause.
English joins the participle λέγουσα ("saying") to the main verb.

11:33.sourceText: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ὡς εἶδεν αὐτὴν κλαίουσαν καὶ τοὺς συνελθόντας αὐτῇ Ἰουδαίους κλαίοντας, ἐνεβριμήσατο τῷ πνεύματι καὶ ἐτάραξεν ἑαυτόν,
11:33.targetText: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled.

groups.note: ἐτάραξεν ἑαυτόν ("troubled himself") is rendered troubled.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds also to the second weeping.

11:34.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν Ποῦ τεθείκατε αὐτόν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Κύριε, ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε.
11:34.targetText: “Where have you put him?” He asked.  “Come and see, Lord,” they answered.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence, so the connective καί is not rendered.
The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:36.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Ἴδε πῶς ἐφίλει αὐτόν.
11:36.targetText: Then the Jews said, “See how He loved him!”

11:37.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπαν Οὐκ ἐδύνατο οὗτος ὁ ἀνοίξας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ποιῆσαι ἵνα καὶ οὗτος μὴ ἀποθάνῃ;
11:37.targetText: But some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?”

groups.note: ἵνα … μή ("so that … not") is rendered kept … from.
The pronoun οὗτος ("this one") is rendered by the name Lazarus.

11:38.sourceText: Ἰησοῦς οὖν πάλιν ἐμβριμώμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔρχεται εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον· ἦν δὲ σπήλαιον, καὶ λίθος ἐπέκειτο ἐπ’ αὐτῷ.
11:38.targetText: Jesus, once again deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone laid across the entrance.

groups.note: καί ("and") is rendered with: a cave with a stone.
The pronoun αὐτῷ ("it") is rendered the entrance.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.
BSB leaves ἐν ἑαυτῷ ("in himself") unexpressed.
BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

11:39.sourceText: λέγει ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἄρατε τὸν λίθον. λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τοῦ τετελευτηκότος Μάρθα Κύριε, ἤδη ὄζει· τεταρταῖος γάρ ἐστιν.
11:39.targetText: “Take away the stone,” Jesus said.  “Lord, by now he stinks,” said Martha, the sister of the dead man. “It has already been four days.”

groups.note: τοῦ τετελευτηκότος ("of the one who had died") is rendered of the dead man.
τεταρταῖος ("a fourth-day one") is rendered four days.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.
BSB starts a new sentence, so γάρ ("for") is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds already; ἤδη is rendered by now.

11:40.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐκ εἶπόν σοι ὅτι ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς ὄψῃ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Θεοῦ;
11:40.targetText: Jesus replied, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?”

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῇ ("to her") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:41.sourceText: ἦραν οὖν τὸν λίθον. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἦρεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἄνω καὶ εἶπεν Πάτερ, εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι ἤκουσάς μου.
11:41.targetText: So they took away the stone. Then Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.

groups.note: The article τούς with ὀφθαλμούς is rendered His.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:42.sourceText: ἐγὼ δὲ ᾔδειν ὅτι πάντοτέ μου ἀκούεις· ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον τὸν περιεστῶτα εἶπον, ἵνα πιστεύσωσιν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.
11:42.targetText: I knew that You always hear Me, but I say this for the benefit of the people standing here, so they may believe that You sent Me.”

groups.note: διά ("because of") is rendered for the benefit of.
τὸν περιεστῶτα ("the one standing around") is rendered standing here.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of say.

11:43.sourceText: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐκραύγασεν Λάζαρε, δεῦρο ἔξω.
11:43.targetText: After Jesus had said this, He called out in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”

groups.note: The participle εἰπών ("having said") is rendered as an After-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject of the participle.

11:44.sourceText: ἐξῆλθεν ὁ τεθνηκὼς δεδεμένος τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας κειρίαις, καὶ ἡ ὄψις αὐτοῦ σουδαρίῳ περιεδέδετο. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἄφετε αὐτὸν ὑπάγειν.
11:44.targetText: The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen, and his face wrapped in a cloth.  “Unwrap him and let him go,” Jesus told them.

targetPhrases.text: The man who had been dead

groups.note: ὁ τεθνηκώς ("the one who had died") is rendered The man who had been dead.
δεδεμένος ("bound") is rendered as the phrase with … bound.
The article τάς with χεῖρας is rendered his.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:45.sourceText: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τὴν Μαριὰμ καὶ θεασάμενοι ὃ ἐποίησεν, ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν·
11:45.targetText: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in Him.

groups.note: BSB's Greek has a different form of the same pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject of ἐποίησεν ("he did").

11:46.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπῆλθον πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους καὶ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς ἃ ἐποίησεν Ἰησοῦς.
11:46.targetText: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.

11:47.sourceText: Συνήγαγον οὖν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συνέδριον, καὶ ἔλεγον Τί ποιοῦμεν, ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος πολλὰ ποιεῖ σημεῖα;
11:47.targetText: Then the chief priests and Pharisees convened the Sanhedrin and said, “What are we to do? This man is performing many signs.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence, so ὅτι ("since") is not rendered.

11:48.sourceText: ἐὰν ἀφῶμεν αὐτὸν οὕτως, πάντες πιστεύσουσιν εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐλεύσονται οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι καὶ ἀροῦσιν ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν τόπον καὶ τὸ ἔθνος.
11:48.targetText: If we let Him go on like this, everyone will believe in Him, and then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”

groups.note: The article τό with ἔθνος is rendered our, repeating ἡμῶν.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb after let.
English adds then to mark the sequence.

11:49.sourceText: εἷς δέ τις ἐξ αὐτῶν Καϊάφας, ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου, εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε οὐδέν,
11:49.targetText: But one of them, named Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all!

groups.note: εἷς τις ("a certain one") is rendered one.
The double negative οὐκ … οὐδέν ("not … nothing") is rendered nothing at all.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the name; the Greek sets Καϊάφας beside "one of them".

11:50.sourceText: οὐδὲ λογίζεσθε ὅτι συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα εἷς ἄνθρωπος ἀποθάνῃ ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ ἔθνος ἀπόληται.
11:50.targetText: You do not realize that it is better for you that one man die for the people than that the whole nation perish.”

groups.note: οὐδέ ("nor") is rendered not.
ἵνα governs both clauses; BSB repeats that.
καὶ μή ("and not") is rendered than.

11:51.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ οὐκ εἶπεν, ἀλλὰ ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου ἐπροφήτευσεν ὅτι ἔμελλεν Ἰησοῦς ἀποθνήσκειν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους,
11:51.targetText: Caiaphas did not say this on his own. Instead, as high priest that year, he was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject of εἶπεν ("he said").

11:52.sourceText: καὶ οὐχ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους μόνον, ἀλλ’ ἵνα καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ Θεοῦ τὰ διεσκορπισμένα συναγάγῃ εἰς ἕν.
11:52.targetText: and not only for the nation, but also for the scattered children of God, to gather them together into one.

groups.note: τὰ διεσκορπισμένα ("the scattered ones") is rendered scattered.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English refers back to the children named earlier in the sentence.
BSB repeats for to set the children beside the nation; in the Greek they are the object of συναγάγῃ ("gather").

11:53.sourceText: ἀπ’ ἐκείνης οὖν τῆς ἡμέρας ἐβουλεύσαντο ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτόν.
11:53.targetText: So from that day on they plotted to kill Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:54.sourceText: Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι παρρησίᾳ περιεπάτει ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν χώραν ἐγγὺς τῆς ἐρήμου, εἰς Ἐφραὶμ λεγομένην πόλιν, κἀκεῖ ἔμεινεν μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν.
11:54.targetText: As a result, Jesus no longer went about publicly among the Jews, but He withdrew to a town called Ephraim in an area near the wilderness. And He stayed there with the disciples.

groups.note: ἀπῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν ("went away from there") is rendered withdrew.
κἀκεῖ is καί ("and") with ἐκεῖ ("there").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:55.sourceText: Ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβησαν πολλοὶ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐκ τῆς χώρας πρὸ τοῦ πάσχα, ἵνα ἁγνίσωσιν ἑαυτούς.
11:55.targetText: Now the Jewish Passover was near, and many people went up from the country to Jerusalem to purify themselves before the Passover.

groups.note: τῶν Ἰουδαίων ("of the Jews") is rendered Jewish.

11:56.sourceText: ἐζήτουν οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἔλεγον μετ’ ἀλλήλων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστηκότες Τί δοκεῖ ὑμῖν; ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν;
11:56.targetText: They kept looking for Jesus and asking one another as they stood in the temple courts, “What do you think? Will He come to the feast at all?”

groups.note: δοκεῖ ὑμῖν ("does it seem to you") is rendered do you think.
BSB turns οὐ μή ("surely not") into the doubting question Will He come … at all?

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB turns the ὅτι-clause into a direct question.

11:57.sourceText: δεδώκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἐντολὰς ἵνα ἐάν τις γνῷ ποῦ ἐστιν μηνύσῃ, ὅπως πιάσωσιν αὐτόν.
11:57.targetText: But the chief priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where He was must report it, so that they could arrest Him.

groups.note: ἐάν τις ("if anyone") is rendered anyone who.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of report.
